papers.title: Baseline Dynamics and Sleep Loss-Driven Changes of Electrocorticographic Aperiodic Properties Are Altered in Mice Lacking Neuroligin-2.
papers.summary: Using Neuroligin-2 knockout mice and multifractal wavelet-leaders analysis of electrocorticographic signals, this study found that Neuroligin-2 shapes cortical aperiodic 1/fβ properties, with knockouts showing increased Hurst exponent (Hm) across wake and sleep states and altered daily dynamics. Sleep deprivation further altered Hm dynamics more in knockouts for wake and paradoxical sleep, and mutants exhibited hypersynchronized epileptic-like events with increased Hm and Dispersion.

papers.title: HIPPIE: a generative model for electrophysiological analysis across species, technologies, and modalities.
authors: Luiz F S Eugenio Dos Santos
papers.summary: The paper introduces HIPPIE, a deep learning generative framework that combines self-supervised pretraining with supervised fine-tuning using conditional convolutional joint autoencoders to classify neurons from extracellular recordings across species, technologies, and modalities. Across mouse, rat, and macaque recordings, HIPPIE classified cell types competitively with existing methods and uniquely enabled counterfactual decoding, cross-species latent interpolation, and cross-modal analysis showing spike-timing and waveform morphology encode largely independent dimensions of neuronal identity.

papers.title: Seizure recruitment properties are dependent upon dynamotype: A modeling study.
papers.summary: Using a two-node Multiclass Epileptor model, the study shows that seizure dynamotype, particularly onset bifurcation, determines recruitment likelihood and speed. Seizures with baseline shifts at onset spread less and slower than those without, while amplitude-scaling onset seizures rarely propagate; human intracranial EEG confirmed unusual recruitment patterns.

papers.title: Computing the geometry of phase-amplitude coupling: A new moment-based framework
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that common phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) metrics are many-to-one mappings, so distinct coupling geometries can yield identical Modulation Index (MI) values. It proposes a circular-moment decomposition that preserves geometric information, validates it in simulations and EEG data showing geometric variability among PAC profiles with matched MI, and applies it to identify differences in delta-low gamma phase geometry in children with developmental language disorder.

papers.title: Diffusion MRI Tractography Predicts Electrophysiological Connectivity and Explains Spectral Signatures of Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain
papers.summary: Combining dMRI tractography and SEEG with single-pulse stimulation in 40 patients, the study found that structural connectivity predicts causal electrophysiological connectivity with high probability (~0.95 for presence, ~0.8 for absence). Direct pathways were marked by early phase-locked broadband activity (10-70 ms), while thalamic indirect pathways showed increased latency (>200 ms) and late oscillations.

papers.title: Stable Network Motifs with Divergent Engagement Across Memory Outcomes
papers.summary: Intracranial EEG in seven epilepsy patients during a visual recognition task showed that successful recognition is characterized by low modularity (Q=0.05), sustained cross-hemispheric integration of left MTL with right prefrontal cortex, and right-hemisphere dominance in directed connectivity (asymmetry index=0.33). Correct rejections instead showed early transient segregation and right-lateralized hubs.

papers.title: Contextual Modulation of Fronto-Central, Parietal, and Global Peak Alpha Frequency.
papers.summary: In 29 healthy participants receiving painful pressure stimuli in reward and punishment contexts, peak alpha frequency (PAF) was significantly lower after incorrect responses in the punishment context (increased pain) compared to correct responses in the same context (maintained pain), despite matched pain intensity. A preliminary cross-context difference in PAF at matched pain intensity was also observed but requires replication.

papers.title: Infants at high and low likelihood for autism show different EEG developmental trajectories in speech tracking and statistical learning.
papers.summary: Longitudinal high-density EEG in 44 infants at high and low likelihood for autism revealed reduced syllable-level neural tracking in high-likelihood infants, correlating with verbal outcomes. High-likelihood infants also showed reduced novelty orientation during word recognition, while multi-talker variability disrupted segmentation in low-likelihood infants but not high-likelihood infants.

papers.title: Time-resolved aperiodic dynamics in event segmentation in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
papers.summary: Using time-resolved spectral parameterization of EEG during movie viewing in 73 adolescents with ADHD and 73 neurotypical controls, the study found that ADHD participants exhibited steeper aperiodic exponents across intervals and exaggerated pre-boundary steepening with attenuated post-boundary flattening around event boundaries. In ADHD only, behavioral segmentation sensitivity correlated with post-boundary aperiodic modulation, linking temporal disorganization to altered aperiodic neural dynamics.

papers.title: Effects of Optic Flow on Electrocortical Dynamics During Walking and Stepping Over Virtual Obstacles.
papers.summary: Using a treadmill-based virtual reality paradigm with EEG, this study found that optic flow during obstacle avoidance enhanced pre-obstacle alpha desynchronization and induced sustained occipital theta synchronization, indicating distinct neural signatures for visual motion processing and motor planning.

papers.title: Lack of vision shifts occipital dynamics toward a frontal-like regime and enhances top-down connectivity
papers.summary: TMS-EEG in 16 blind and 16 sighted individuals showed that blindness shifts occipital cortex dynamics toward a faster, lower-amplitude frontal-like regime and specifically enhances frontal-to-occipital effective connectivity. Faster occipital dynamics correlated with stronger top-down frontal recruitment, linking local temporal retuning to network integration.

papers.title: Comprehensive deep representation-based Wasserstein domain discriminator for cross-subject motor imagery EEG classification.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a Comprehensive Deep Representation-based Wasserstein Domain Discriminator (CDR-WDD) for cross-subject motor imagery EEG classification, achieving average accuracies of 84.34%, 89.59%, 73.32%, and 87.75% on four benchmark datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art domain adaptation models.

papers.title: Anticipated distractor processing relies on distinct representational states before and after distractor onset in visual working memory
papers.summary: Using human EEG and multivariate decoding, this study tracked anticipatory and post-onset distractor representations in visual working memory, finding that pre-distractor coding was content-specific but not linked to behavioral protection, whereas post-distractor reformatting into a less stable representational state was associated with reduced interference. The results indicate a temporally coordinated control mechanism in which anticipatory coding specifies upcoming irrelevant content and post-onset representational instability implements protection.

papers.title: Exploiting frontotemporal asymmetry in low-channel EEG emotion recognition via spectral fusion network.
papers.summary: The paper proposes the Spatiotemporal Spectral Asymmetric Fusion Network (STSANet), a dual-branch model that explicitly quantifies frontotemporal hemispheric asymmetry and fuses spectral oscillations for low-channel EEG emotion recognition. It achieved accuracies of 86.80% on SEED and 87.43% on a self-collected dataset, with robustness in trial-level cross-validation and confirmed dependence on spatial asymmetry modeling.

papers.title: Effect of stimulation parameters for transcranial temporal interference stimulation to enhance occipital alpha-oscillations in healthy participants
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, sham- and carrier-controlled within-subject study, 20-minute transcranial temporal interference stimulation at individual alpha frequency significantly increased occipital alpha power compared with both high-frequency carrier and sham stimulation, with no behavioral effects. The findings support frequency-specific modulation of cortical oscillations by temporal interference rather than high-frequency carrier components alone.

papers.title: A Neural Network with Multi-Type Attention for Enhancing Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: This paper introduces MTANet, an end-to-end neural network with multi-type attention that extracts spatiotemporal-frequency coupling features for motor imagery EEG decoding, achieving average accuracies of 83.39% on BCI IV IIa, 89.47% on BCI IV IIb, and 77.06% on BCI III IIIa, outperforming seven state-of-the-art models.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Monitoring for Seizure Risk Stratification in the Critically III.
papers.summary: This review outlines the role of continuous EEG for diagnosing electrographic seizures and epileptiform abnormalities in critically ill patients and describes risk-stratification approaches, including the validated 2HELPS2B score, to optimize monitoring duration and resource use. It emphasizes that many ICU seizures are clinically silent and that risk-guided cEEG can improve efficiency in critical care.

papers.title: Phase-lag-dependent modulation of interhemispheric β-band functional connectivity by dual-site tACS
papers.summary: In 23 healthy participants, dual-site 20 Hz tACS over bilateral M1s with varying phase-lags induced transient (first 5 s) and frequency-specific (18–22 Hz) modulation of interhemispheric beta functional connectivity without affecting spectral power; the magnitude related quadratically to individual beta-peak frequency.

papers.title: Neurofeedback-Guided Motor Imagery in Chronic Stroke: A Case Series on Upper-Limb Recovery, Cortical Activation, and Brain Symmetry.
papers.summary: This double-blind, controlled case series examined EEG-based brain-computer interface neurofeedback combined with motor imagery and a four-week physiotherapy program in seven chronic stroke patients. Participants receiving real neurofeedback showed improvements exceeding minimal clinically important difference thresholds in at least one functional outcome, most notably grip strength, along with more symmetrical EEG activity and more consistent sensorimotor and cerebellar fMRI activation patterns than sham controls.

papers.title: Auditory stimuli extend the temporal window of visual integration by modulating alpha-band oscillations
papers.summary: EEG and tACS experiments showed that a brief auditory stimulus widens the temporal integration window for successive visual flashes by transiently reducing poststimulus instantaneous alpha frequency, with individual alpha-cycle lengthening correlating with fusion threshold prolongation, and a phase-resetting model reproduced the findings.

papers.title: Association between abnormal theta oscillation-default mode network functional connectivity and internet addiction behavior in adolescent depression patients: a resting-state EEG study.
papers.summary: In 183 drug-naive first-episode adolescent MDD patients and 93 healthy controls, abnormal theta oscillation–default mode network functional connectivity was associated with internet addiction severity. Theta oscillation mediated the relationship between anhedonia and IA severity, and theta band power spectral density was lower in the IA group than in the MDD group.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging using a familial temporal lobe epilepsy model in cats: an exploratory methodological pilot study.
papers.summary: This exploratory methodological pilot study implemented simultaneous EEG-fMRI in cats with familial spontaneous epilepsy and identified amygdalo-hippocampal BOLD activation in 16/30 sessions using small-volume correction, but individual-level epileptogenic zone localization remained insufficient for clinical use.

papers.title: Transcranial rotating permanent magnet stimulation for focal continuous spike-and-wave during sleep: First-in-human pediatric pilot study.
papers.summary: In this first-in-human pediatric pilot study, a single 10-minute session of focal transcranial rotating permanent magnet stimulation (TRPMS) in 10 children with focal continuous spike-and-wave during sleep was safe and well tolerated. Mean sleep spike-wave index decreased significantly (e.g., from 90.6% to 81.7% for reviewer 1, p=0.0186) and mean awake SWI also decreased significantly, providing preliminary proof-of-concept evidence.

papers.title: Personalized Brain Stimulation based on Brain Oscillations: A Systematic Review of MEG- and EEG-informed Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (tACS).
papers.summary: This systematic review characterized 143 experiments from 78 publications on MEG/EEG-informed personalized transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS). Frequency-based individualization predominated (93%, mostly alpha at 69.2%), and 77.9% of sham-controlled experiments reported significant positive outcomes, whereas only 56.2% of active-controlled experiments did.

papers.title: Precision Sedation for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in Older Adults: Brain Vulnerability and Recovery.
papers.summary: This review discusses precision sedation for gastrointestinal endoscopy in older adults, covering age-related brain vulnerability, sedative options such as propofol, remimazolam, ciprofol, and dexmedetomidine, and monitoring with processed EEG, cerebral oximetry, and capnography. It emphasizes aiming for minimum effective sedation depth and notes that short-term outcome improvements should not be assumed to prevent postoperative delirium or longer-term cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Millifluidic triMEA organoid platform with stretchable microelectrode arrays for parallel organoid electrophysiology under standardized perfusion.
papers.summary: The paper presents a triMEA millifluidic platform integrating three stretchable microelectrode arrays in one device to provide uniform perfusion across three independent wells, enabling simultaneous electrophysiological recordings from three human midbrain organoids. Computational and experimental validation confirmed stable fluidic profiles and successful parallel recordings under continuous perfusion.

papers.title: Drug screen and machine learning predict neuroprotective agents in a preclinical human model of childhood dementia.
papers.summary: Using patient-derived iPSCs from children with Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IIIA, the study established a human cortical model recapitulating lysosomal dysfunction, heparan sulfate accumulation, neurodegeneration, and astrocytic reactivity. A multimodal drug screen integrating machine learning, confocal imaging, single-nuclei transcriptomics, and electrophysiology identified at least nine repurposed compounds that significantly mitigated these phenotypes within two weeks in vitro.

papers.title: Neural Responsivity to Unexpected Stimuli Moderates a Developmental Pathway to Anxiety: A Community-Sample Replication in Early Infancy and Childhood
papers.summary: In 147 infants from a community sample, the mismatch response (MMR) at 4 months moderated the pathways from negative reactivity to behavioral inhibition at 14 months and from behavioral inhibition to anxiety symptoms at 30 months. More negative MMR was associated with stronger risk pathways, whereas no significant associations were found at more positive MMR levels; anxiety symptoms were stable from 30 months to 4-6 years.

papers.title: Spatial heterogeneity of APD under long QT conditions: characterisation and relationship to sinus activation sequence.
papers.summary: Optical mapping in Langendorff-perfused rabbit hearts showed a strong inverse relationship between sinus activation time and APD90, and dofetilide-induced IKr blockade or longer pacing cycle lengths increased APD prolongation at earlier-activated sites, enhancing spatial APD heterogeneity. Isolated myocytes and mRNA measurements indicated that sites with different sinus activation times have distinct intrinsic APD and ion-channel gene expression profiles.

papers.title: Valproate-Associated Hyperammonemic Encephalopathy Despite Nontoxic Serum Levels and Preserved Liver Function: A Case Report.
papers.summary: The paper reports a 49-year-old man with drug-resistant epilepsy who developed valproate-associated hyperammonemic encephalopathy (VHE) despite therapeutic or subtherapeutic valproate levels and preserved liver function. Valproate withdrawal led to sustained neurological recovery and a decrease in serum ammonia from 126.5 to 43.1 µmol/L.

papers.title: Probable Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease Presenting as Rapidly Progressive Dementia: A Case Report From Georgia.
papers.summary: The paper describes a 53-year-old man from Georgia with probable sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease presenting as rapidly progressive dementia, gait ataxia, and other neurological signs. Diagnosis was supported by a positive CSF 14-3-3 protein result and MRI restricted diffusion in the left caudate nucleus, but the patient died approximately seven months after symptom onset.

papers.title: A Four-Year Diagnostic Journey to Acute Intermittent Porphyria in a 19-Year-Old Woman: Lessons on Recognizing Neurovisceral Clues.
papers.summary: The paper reports a 19-year-old woman with a four-year history of recurrent seizures and abdominal pain who was ultimately diagnosed with acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) after fecal total porphyrins were found elevated at 72.3 nmol/g. It emphasizes that normal urinary porphyrin levels outside an acute attack do not exclude AIP and that fecal porphyrin analysis can provide complementary evidence.

papers.title: Photochemical degradation of azo textile dyes by UV/H2O2 advanced oxidation process: kinetic, parametric and mechanistic insights.
papers.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
papers.summary: This study investigated UV/H2O2 advanced oxidation for degrading two azo textile dyes, Solophenyl Blue and Cibacron Blue, optimizing parameters such as pH and H2O2 dosage and achieving up to 99.8% removal after 180 minutes under acidic conditions. Degradation followed pseudo-first-order kinetics, and DFT calculations indicated that Solophenyl Blue has greater electron-donating capacity and susceptibility to hydroxyl radical attack than Cibacron Blue.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
